Name: Modern European
Description: The broad current of European philosophy from the Renaissance through the 20th century, spanning Rationalism, Empiricism, Idealism, and Continental and Analytic traditions.

Name: American
Description: The philosophical tradition of the United States, from early Pragmatism through 20th-century Analytic and public philosophy.

Name: Latin Christian
Description: The Latin-speaking Christian intellectual world of medieval and early modern Europe, centered on Scholasticism and the Church.

Name: Classical Chinese
Description: The foundational period of Chinese philosophy, including Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, and Legalism.

Name: Ancient Greek
Description: The philosophy of the Greek city-states from the Presocratics through Aristotle.

Name: Indian Buddhist
Description: The Buddhist philosophical schools that developed on the Indian subcontinent, from early Buddhism through Madhyamaka and Yogācāra.

Name: Islamic
Description: The philosophical tradition of the medieval Islamic world, synthesizing Greek philosophy with Islamic theology and law.

Name: Indian Hindu
Description: The Hindu philosophical schools of the Indian subcontinent, including Vedānta, Yoga, Sāṃkhya, and Nyāya.

Name: Ancient Roman
Description: The Latin philosophical culture of the Roman Republic and Empire, especially its adaptations of Greek Stoicism and Epicureanism.

Name: Neo-Confucian
Description: The medieval and early-modern Chinese revival and metaphysical elaboration of classical Confucian ethics.

Name: African
Description: Continental African philosophical traditions and movements, including African Socialism and Pan-Africanism.

Name: Latin American
Description: 20th-century Latin American philosophy, often engaging liberation theology, indigenous thought, and postcolonial critique.

Name: Ancient Greek (Hellenistic)
Description: The Greek philosophical culture of the Hellenistic period following Alexander's conquests, including Stoicism, Epicureanism, and Skepticism.

Name: Jewish
Description: The philosophical tradition growing out of Jewish religious and intellectual life, from medieval rationalism to modern Jewish thought.

Name: Italian
Description: The philosophical culture of Renaissance and early modern Italy, especially civic and political humanism.

Name: Buddhist (Zen)
Description: The Zen Buddhist tradition, especially as it developed in medieval and modern Japan.

Name: Indian Jain
Description: The Jain philosophical tradition of the Indian subcontinent, centered on non-violence and its distinctive pluralist metaphysics.

Name: Caribbean/African
Description: The philosophical and political thought of the African diaspora in the Caribbean, especially Pan-African and anti-colonial thought.

Name: Canadian
Description: The philosophical tradition of English and French Canada within the broader North American academic context.

Name: Western
Description: A general label for philosophers working within the broad modern Western tradition without a more specific national or civilizational tag.
